angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 10,667,168 km at 80.91 pc = 1.76 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48356: distance 80.906 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.021), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 80.906 +/- 1.699 pc; Gaia DR3 gives this source no parallax (a two-parameter solution)
radiusSource: Radius 15.333 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48356: radius 15.333 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 140.555 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.054) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 10,667,168 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5079 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48356: effective temperature 5079 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.04) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48356: effective temperature 5079 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.04) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 556) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
